requirements.requirement: Repair the bundle links as relative symbolic links that resolve to the intended targets recorded in links.tsv.
requirements.summary: Both links remain symbolic links, use relative targets, and resolve exactly to the manifest-defined objects. Their data is accessible through the repaired links, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the bundle continues to work when copied to another directory.
requirements.summary: A bounded copy test placed the bundle at a different nested path; both links resolved within the copied bundle and returned the expected report content.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the bundle's regular files while repairing only the links.
requirements.summary: The two regular files retained their baseline SHA-256 hashes, sizes, modes, ownership, and readable contents before and after repair and restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged after execution and reboot. The implementation used existing platform utilities, with no package or platform modification shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the node was temporarily unreachable, a different boot ID was observed, and system, link, file, and data health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Native package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently compared; no package-changing command is present.
Final regular-file checks did not re-record mtimes, although hashes, sizes, modes, ownership, and contents were preserved and no command targeted those files.
The retained /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log was inventoried but its contents and permissions were not captured.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The substantive mutations were narrowly connected to the task: replacing the two symlink targets, creating and removing a temporary relocation-test copy, and performing the mandatory restart. The failed manifest-parsing and unprivileged replacement attempts show no state change. One minor unnecessary retained mutation was identified: cmd-36d67ac3286c48e6 redirected reboot output to /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, which remained after completion. No failed services, new listening exposures, or other harmful residue were observed. Reboot-related PID and systemd-private-directory changes are expected lifecycle effects.
